interview.hardest_part: Navigating Pharloom from single screenshots with no map memory, and then executing precise platforming and multi-hit boss fights under 0.4-second committed inputs. Moss Mother and the Bell Beast gate real progress and demand sustained dodging, while the later milestones (Deep Docks, Swift Step, Citadel) need long correct route chains through rooms I cannot reliably recognise twice.
interview.likely_failure: Getting stuck in a room whose exit is off-screen or requires a precise jump/dash, burning the wall-clock budget on trial-and-error, or dying repeatedly to Moss Mother and being sent back to the last bench with no silk and no bench respawn recorded. Any wrong turn costs many steps and there is only one attempt.
interview.helpful_mechanics: Holding a direction for a full 0.4 s gives smooth, forgiving continuous movement; the needle attack can be spammed while moving; death respawns at a bench rather than restarting the run, so mistakes are recoverable; and many milestones are cheap and early - scene visits, journal kill counts, shell shards, rosaries, a collectable, and meeting a character - so points accrue even without deep progress. Resting at a bench also restores health and sets a checkpoint.
interview.harmful_mechanics: Each action is a discrete 0.4 s commitment with no mid-step correction, which makes short hops, dash timing and boss dodges clumsy; hazards and enemies deal contact damage while Hornet's masks are few; silk only refills by landing hits so binds are unreliable under pressure; the map is not visible and rooms look similar across screenshots; and thinking time counts against the three-hour budget.
